newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Ameritech EPS up without long-distance.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Ameritech EPS up without long-distance.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday its first quarter earnings and revenues rose despite regulatory problems with entering the long-distance market.
"We've not been allowed into the long-distance business as of yet, which we were frankly counting on," chief financial officer Oren Shaffer said in an interview.
Ameritech reported that first quarter income rose 12.1 percent to $536 million and revenues grew 8.2 percent to $3.86 billion.
"We clearly want to be in the long distance business," Shaffer said. "It would significantly enhance our revenue growth."
Ameritech estimates the long-distance market in its five-state area at $9 billion.
It said it has now achieved double-digit earnings growth, a long-standing goal, for 14 consecutive quarters.

Ameritech has addressed the regulatory issues and will seek long distance approval in Michigan by the end of April or early May. Shaffer said he hopes to offer long distance service in all of Ameritech's five states by the end of 1997.
He said Ameritech is feeling pressure from other companies providing short-distance toll calls within its region, but that should subside once it enters the long-distance market.
"The sooner we're allowed onto the playing field, then we'll see how stiff that competition is, but right now the competition is one-sided," he said.
Analysts have questioned the regional Bells' ability to handle competition in their local markets -- a requirement of their entering the lucrative long-distance market.
But Shaffer said Ameritech is confident.
"The consumers know us as a company supplying their service...it would seem to me that we have a better reason to ask that consumer to trust us to supply all of their communications needs," he said.
Shaffer does not expect severe pricing pressure in the local market.
"We think there is a real value equation here and there is also substantial growth in this market," Shaffer said. "We think any kind of outright price war is probably avoidable."

Analysts say Ameritech's access line growth has fallen in recent quarters. New line growth in the first quarter was 3.2 percent versus 3.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 and 3.7 percent in the third.

But Shaffer said the company is focusing more on high-margin call management services, such as call waiting and caller ID, which grew by 26 percent over last year. He said that level of growth is sustainable.
"We think we have the puzzle figured out -- how to do access lines, call features, and stick to the high-revenue side of things," Shaffer said.
He said industry penetration in those markets is low and affords ample opportunity for future growth.

"We're targetting our additional line growth to where it will lead to better possibilities of selling the higher-margin services, and that seems to be a very powerful combination which is working very well for us," he said.
((--Chicago newsdesk, 312-408-8787))
